themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints surged to 4 reports THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over 8 weeks (1500% spike, z-score 8.66), signaling a potential acute environmental hazard affecting housing stock in Fordham/University Heights that demands immediate investigation of source and affected buildings.
evidence: 4 lead complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 average per week over prior 8 weeks (1500% increase)
Z-score of 8.66 indicates statistically extreme outlier event
Community board has standing air quality and environmental complaint requests, suggesting environmental consciousness in district
reporting_angles: Which buildings or addresses generated the 4 complaints? Are they clustered (renovation-related) or dispersed?
Interview DOH and DEP on what triggered the spike—renovation work, water testing, or resident-initiated testing?

themes_detail.label: Special Projects Inspection surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK from 0.4 weekly baseline (1233% spike, z-score 6.65), suggesting concentrated inspection activity or enforcement action in the district that may signal code violations or conditions prompting official scrutiny.
evidence: 5 SPIT complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 average per week over prior 8 weeks (1233% increase)
Z-score of 6.65 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
DOB shows 254 total filings in past 90 days (139 alterations), suggesting active construction/compliance activity
reporting_angles: What triggered SPIT deployment THIS WEEK—scheduled sweeps, complaints, or specific violation patterns?
Cross-reference SPIT complaints with DOB alteration permits to identify if renovation work is driving inspections

themes_detail.label: Drinking complaint spike resolved
themes_detail.summary: Drinking complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 3 reports (2300% above 8-week baseline of 0.1), but this elevated level appears to have subsided; this historical spike warrants a brief check-in on whether conditions at a specific location (park, transit hub, street corner) were addressed.
evidence: 3 drinking complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (2300% spike)
Spike appears resolved (no current-week elevation), suggesting temporary condition or intervention
reporting_angles: Were the 3 complaints from the same location or same incident? Did NYPD or Parks enforce?
Did city intervention (increased police presence, park closure, etc.) resolve the spike 3 weeks ago?

themes_detail.label: Street noise elevated 3 weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 263 reports 3 weeks ago from 69.1 weekly average (280% increase, z-score 3.82), likely driven by temporary construction or events; current status unclear but worth confirming whether the spike has subsided or persists.
evidence: 263 street/sidewalk noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 69.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (280% spike)
Current week data needed to assess whether spike was temporary or sustained
reporting_angles: What construction, road work, or events occurred 3 weeks ago that triggered the complaint surge?
Has the spike resolved this week, or is street noise a persistent issue in specific commercial/industrial corridors?

themes_detail.label: Heat complaints remain elevated
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints (4,005 over 90 days) remain the single highest complaint volume in the district, suggesting a chronic housing maintenance crisis; while not a new spike, the persistent scale warrants investigation into landlord compliance and tenant conditions ahead of winter heating season.
evidence: 4,005 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days (44.5 per day, 311 per week) vastly exceed other complaint categories
Represents 23% of all 311 complaints in district over 3-month period
Pattern repeats year after year, indicating systemic landlord non-compliance rather than weather or infrastructure event
reporting_angles: Profile 2-3 buildings with persistent heat complaints; name landlords and violations on record
Interview tenants on how lack of heat affects families, elderly residents, and health; document actual temperatures inside units
